post.title: Swapping crypto? The IRS counts it as a sale
post.ig:
Swapped one coin for another? The IRS calls that a sale.

The IRS treats crypto as property, so selling, swapping, spending or getting paid in it can all be taxable.
Example: $1,000 of bitcoin grows to $1,500, you swap it for ether: that's a $500 gain, about $110 of tax at a 22% short-term rate or $75 at the 15% long-term rate.
In 2026, single filers with taxable income up to $49,450 pay 0% on long-term gains.
Since 2025, exchanges report crypto sales to the IRS on Form 1099-DA.

Sources: IRS digital asset FAQ, IRS Topic 409, IRS 2026 inflation adjustments.
